newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical reduces price for Circon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical reduces price for Circon.

text.p: United States Surgical Corp. Monday reduced its hostile cash takeover offer for Circon Corp. to $17 a share, or about $217 million, citing Circon's disappointing third-quarter earnings.
U.S. Surgical, which launched an $18-a-share bid worth about $230 on Aug. 2, also extended its offer for Circon, another surgical products company, through Feb. 13.
The original offer was 83 percent percent higher than the average closing price of Circon's common stock during the past 10 trading days, U.S. Surgical said.
Circon fell 87.5 cents to $15.50 on Nasdaq at mid-morning. Norwalk, Conn.-based U.S. Surgical edged down 25 cents to $39 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"With the passage of time, not only has Circon's management been unable to achieve better operating results, but Circon's performance continues to be below even historical levels," said Leon C. Hirsch, chairman and CEO of U.S. Surgical.

On Oct. 25, Circon reported a loss of $1.5 million, or 11 cents a share, in the third quarter, compared with a loss of $7.4 million, or 56 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales fell to $38.4 million to $42.1 million.
"This performance demonstrates that Circon's management has been unable to deliver to their shareholders the turnaround it has been promising," Hirsch said.
"Moreover, management has strapped its shareholders with an even greater burden through the heavy expenditure of $3.2 million for a defence-related charge."

U.S. Surgical said it now owns 79 percent of Circon shares not held by Circon's management and board, including 7.7 million shares tendered as of Friday. U.S. Surgical previously owned 1 million Circon shares, or about 8 percent of the Santa Barbara, Calif.-based company.

Within the past 10 days, U.S. Surgical again offered to meet with Circon's management to discuss in detail proposals for the merger. "They refused such a meeting, stating that Circon was not for sale," U.S. Surgical said.
Circon management has adopted a poison pill and golden parachutes to defend itself against the hostile bid.
